entry.title: Do Flow-Generation Tools Matter? Unsupervised Characterization of MQTT Traffic Across Public Datasets
entry.summary:
Message Queue Telemetry Transport (MQTT) is widely used in IoT environments due to its lightweight publish-subscribe design and suitability for resource-constrained networks. While current MQTT security studies mainly focus on detecting attacks and optimizing classification performance, this work takes a different perspective by presenting a cross-dataset, tool-aware characterization of MQTT traffic at the flow level. This perspective is motivated by the fact that flow-generation is tool-dependent: flows are not directly observed in packet captures, but are constructed through tool-specific decisions about packet grouping, flow termination, and feature export.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #networking #cryptography

entry.title: MASAR: Multi-stage Attack Surface Analysis and Reasoning Framework for Telecom Networks
entry.summary:
The increasing complexity of modern telecommunications networks introduces security challenges that require systematic threat analysis. However, a gap remains between architectural threat modeling frameworks, such as Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, and Elevation of Privilege (STRIDE), and operational knowledge bases, such as the MITRE Five-G Hierarchy of Threats (FiGHT). This gap limits the ability to connect architectural weaknesses with specific protocol behaviors and attack sequences.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #cryptography #networking

entry.title: GhostFaceMPC: Privacy-Preserving Face Recognition with Multi-Party Computation
entry.summary:
Facial recognition has become central to modern authentication systems, security frameworks, and personalized services. However, its widespread adoption is hindered by severe privacy risks, particularly surrounding unauthorized access to sensitive biometric data. To address these challenges, this paper presents GhostFaceMPC, the first end-to-end, privacy-preserving face recognition system to evaluate a deep convolutional neural network extractor and matching under secure multi-party computation.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #neuroscience #inference

entry.title: A Unified Evaluation Framework of Physical Adversarial Robustness in the Edge VLM Era
entry.summary:
Recent advancements in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) enable end-to-end visual grounding via language prompts and generative decoding, demonstrating largely improved zero-shot and open-vocabulary detection capabilities. As a result, VLMs are rapidly being deployed at the edge in safety-critical real-world systems. However, the physical adversarial robustness of edge VLMs has not been systematically studied, and the fundamental differences in output with modern object detectors create methodological challenges for fair evaluation.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #computer-vision #ml-theory

entry.title: Graphs and cycles in curve-based collision walks. In this work, we look at collision-based attacks both for elliptic curve and isogeny problems.
entry.summary:
In this work, we look at collision-based attacks both for elliptic curve and isogeny problems. Our main focus is on attacks in the multi-user setting, i.e., where one tries to recover all secret keys of a large set of $L$ public keys simultaneously, in a faster way than the total time required to attack each key individually. We consider three different problems: (1) the discrete logarithm problem on elliptic curves, (2) the isogeny pathfinding problem on supersingular $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$-curves, (3) the isogeny pathfinding problem on supersingular $\mathbb{F}_p$-curves.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics

entry.title: One-Step Schnorr Threshold Identification
entry.summary:
Threshold cryptographic primitives have not been widely adopted in real-world distributed systems (i.e., beyond the closed committee model) presumably due to state-synchronization overhead and complex certification processes for the shareholders. These are both aspects of their overreliance on infrastructure, an assumption that is usually glossed over in their design. In this work, we propose OSST, a real-time threshold identification protocol that achieves non-interactivity and non-reliance on public shares by means of direct proof interpolation.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust #distributed-systems

entry.title: A New Approach to Reducing Modulus Requirements in Homomorphic Computation: Precision Allocation in CKKS
entry.summary:
Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables computation over encrypted data subject to the prescribed security and precision requirements (allowable deviations from ideal results). Among all FHE schemes, CKKS is a representative scheme for approximate arithmetic, allowing the same operation on multiple values packed into a single RLWE ciphertext. Reducing ciphertext modulus $Q$ for given output precision requirements under RLWE security constraints is a central challenge in homomorphic computation.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics

entry.title: Rotational-Quasidifferential Framework - A Geometric Approach to Rotational-XOR Cryptanalysis
entry.summary:
Rotational-XOR (RX) cryptanalysis extends rotational cryptanalysis by combining rotational relations with XOR translations, enabling the analysis of symmetric-key primitives even in the presence of symmetry-breaking constants. Existing analyses of RX characteristics, however, typically rely on independence assumptions when estimating characteristic probabilities, which may lead to inaccurate probability evaluations and even incompatible characteristics. In this paper, we introduce the first application of the geometric approach to RX cryptanalysis.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp
